standard_prerequisites.name: Cut rank
standard_prerequisites.statement: The rank of a cut is the size of the cut formula; the maximal rank of a proof is the largest rank of its cuts.
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof stratifies cuts by rank d and counts n the cuts of maximal rank (754-756).

standard_prerequisites.name: Maximal cut reduction
standard_prerequisites.statement: A topmost cut of maximal rank in a G3c proof can be replaced so that the end-sequent is unchanged and all cuts in the replaced part have strictly smaller rank; the unit proves this as its own lemma.
standard_prerequisites.use: It performs the replacement step in the inner induction (758-762).

standard_prerequisites.name: Topmost cut
standard_prerequisites.statement: A cut is topmost when no cut of the same or greater rank occurs above it in the proof tree.
standard_prerequisites.use: Picking a topmost cut of rank d ensures the replacement does not disturb other maximal cuts above it (758-759).

core_obligations: Let d be the maximal cut rank in pi and n the number of cuts of rank d; prove by induction on n that all rank-d cuts can be removed: if n is zero there is nothing to do, otherwise pick a topmost rank-d cut, replace its subproof by the reduced proof of the same end-sequent with cuts of rank below d, leaving n-1 cuts of rank d for the induction hypothesis (754-764).

Then prove the theorem by induction on d: if d is zero all cuts are atomic and the inner statement removes them all; if d is greater, the inner statement converts all rank-d cuts into cuts of rank below d, so the maximal rank strictly drops and the induction hypothesis applies (766-771).
Conclude that pi transforms into a proof in G3c with no cut rule at all (753-771).

proof_roadmap.step: Remove all cuts of maximal rank by induction on their number, replacing a topmost one via the reduction lemma.
Remove the remaining ranks by induction on the maximal rank.

difficulty_reason: The counted theorem is the author theorem at source lines 749-751: every proof in G3c plus the cut rule can be transformed into a cut-free G3c proof. The author proof (753-771) is a genuine double induction: first it removes all cuts of maximal rank by induction on their number, replacing a topmost maximal cut through the unit's reduction lemma and lowering the count, then it removes all ranks by induction on the maximal rank itself. Managing the two nested induction hypotheses and seeing why the topmost-cut replacement strictly decreases either the rank or the count is the load-bearing work; the rank-reduction step itself is delegated to the separately proved reduction lemma of the same unit.
